tables.title: Moves
rows: It thrusts out one hand, then the other, and each one releases a fan of orbs spread across 80 degrees. The orbs fly straight at a tenth of a Pillager arrow's speed and break on walls, so step through the gaps or put cover between you.

It only casts this when you're close. The regular Evoker's trap-summon sound plays, and after a slow wind-up seven fangs erupt in a ring around it; each hits for 15, knocks you back and applies Slowed, so roll out of the ring as soon as you hear the cue.

A bubble forms around it and takes every hit meant for the Evoker until it has absorbed 50 damage (up to 1.75 times that with four players). A new bubble can't go up until 23 seconds after the last one did, so popping it fast buys a longer window on the boss.

Between 95% and 60% health it calls in a squad of 1-2 Pillagers, 2-6 Vindicators, up to 2 Royal Guards and sometimes an Enchanter, with no more than six alive from this spell. It can recast every 26 seconds.
Below 60% health the squad is replaced by a bigger wave: four Vex, 1-2 Pillagers, 1-2 Royal Guards and an Enchanter, with up to 12 alive at once. It can recast every 32 seconds.

Only while its bubble is down and it's above 15% health, it fades out and reappears at a random flee point in the arena, at most once every 15 seconds. It's untargetable and invulnerable for about half a second as it vanishes.
Once its health drops below 15%, it teleports to the center of the arena a single time. It has already stopped chasing you at 25% and no longer retreats, so it finishes the fight from that spot.
